description: Golden-question retrieval eval set for Loopctl.Knowledge.search_combined/3. Line 1 is the header; every other line is one labeled question with its own self-contained corpus. See Loopctl.Knowledge.RetrievalEval.GoldenSet for the field schema and docs/runbooks/retrieval_eval.md for how to add a question.

question: how do I enable row level security on a new tenant scoped table
source: hand-authored from the tenancy-rls domain skill

corpus.title: Enable row level security on every new tenant table
corpus.body: Every new tenant scoped table must declare ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, never FORCE, because the production schema_admin role owns the table without BYPASSRLS.

corpus.title: Tenant isolation policy shape for row level security
corpus.body: The row level security policy compares tenant_id against the current_setting for the request, so every query is isolated per tenant.

corpus.title: Adding a composite index to a large table
corpus.body: Create indexes concurrently on large tables so a migration does not take a long exclusive lock on production.

corpus.title: Adding a value to an Ecto enum column
corpus.body: Ecto enums are stored as strings, so adding a value only requires updating the schema and any validation.

question: why does reporting a story done return self report blocked
source: hand-authored from the chain-of-custody domain skill

corpus.title: Self report blocked is the custody gate working
corpus.body: Reporting a story done fails with self report blocked when the reporting key shares dispatch lineage with the implementer, which is the chain of custody gate working as designed.

corpus.title: Dispatch lineage is resolved server side
corpus.body: The reporter dispatch lineage is resolved from the authenticating key and compared against the implementer lineage, never supplied by the client.

corpus.title: Role hierarchy for read endpoints
corpus.body: Higher roles can reach lower role read endpoints whenever the plug uses the role option rather than exact_role.

corpus.title: Webhook subscription events
corpus.body: A webhook subscription selects the event types the endpoint receives and may use a wildcard.

question: how should an oban worker back off between retries
source: hand-authored from the oban patterns skill

corpus.title: Jittered exponential backoff for an Oban worker
corpus.body: Override backoff on the Oban worker to compute an exponential delay with jitter so retries from many jobs do not synchronize into a thundering herd.

corpus.title: Discard versus error in an Oban worker
corpus.body: Return discard for a permanent failure and error for a retryable failure so the queue does not burn attempts on work that can never succeed.

corpus.title: Unique Oban jobs keyed on args
corpus.body: Declare unique with the args and period so the same job is not enqueued twice within the window.

corpus.title: Broadway is not a job queue
corpus.body: Broadway consumes external queues such as SQS or Kafka and is the wrong tool for database backed background jobs.

question: how do I inject a mock http client into a context for tests
source: hand-authored from the elixir patterns skill

corpus.title: Config based dependency injection with a behaviour
corpus.body: Define a behaviour, resolve the implementation through Application.get_env in the consumer, and map the test environment to a Mox mock in config/test.exs.

corpus.title: Never call Application.put_env inside a test
corpus.body: Swapping an implementation with Application.put_env breaks async test isolation, so all service swapping happens through config/test.exs instead.

corpus.title: Fixtures live in one support file
corpus.body: Every fixture and build helper is defined only in test/support/fixtures.ex so a schema change updates one place.

corpus.title: Sandbox mode and external processes
corpus.body: A GenServer outside the test process does not share the sandbox transaction, so it cannot see rows the test inserted.

question: what does search mode keyword only with fallback true mean
source: hand-authored from combined search meta

corpus.title: Keyword only fallback carries a bounded fallback reason
corpus.body: When the query embedding cannot be generated, combined search degrades to keyword only and the meta carries fallback true plus a bounded fallback reason tag naming why.

corpus.title: The no embedding key fallback reason
corpus.body: A missing embedding provider key produces the no_embedding_key fallback reason and the response leads with a remediation notice.

corpus.title: Semantic search returned nothing
corpus.body: When the embedding succeeded but semantic ranking returned no rows, the meta carries a semantic result count of zero and fallback stays false.

corpus.title: Combined search weights must sum to one
corpus.body: The keyword weight and semantic weight must sum to one within a small tolerance or combined search returns invalid weights.

question: how does an agent get a short lived api key for one dispatch
source: hand-authored from chain of custody v2

corpus.title: Per dispatch ephemeral keys replace long lived env keys
corpus.body: Minting a dispatch returns an ephemeral api key with a bounded time to live plus the lineage path from root to self, replacing long lived environment variable keys.

corpus.title: The lineage path of a dispatch
corpus.body: Each dispatch records the ordered path of ancestor dispatch ids so a shared lineage prefix can be detected when a custody gate runs.

corpus.title: Capability tokens are scoped and non replayable
corpus.body: A capability token is signed, scoped to one action, and carries a nonce so it cannot be replayed.

corpus.title: Creating an api key over the http api
corpus.body: The http api key create path excludes the superadmin role so a key cannot self promote past its creator.

question: which repo should a vector search query use
source: hand-authored from the tenancy-rls domain skill

corpus.title: Route heavy and vector reads through the HeavyRead facade
corpus.body: Heavy analytical and vector reads go through the HeavyRead facade rather than Repo or AdminRepo so the dedicated bypassrls pool absorbs them.

corpus.title: Why the admin pool starves under a heavy read
corpus.body: The admin repo runs a very small connection pool, so routing a long vector scan through it starves custody writes.

corpus.title: The RLS enforced repo
corpus.body: The default repo enforces row level security by setting the tenant local to each transaction.

corpus.title: Prepared statements and pgbouncer
corpus.body: Use unnamed prepare with pgbouncer so parameterized queries keep working without server side prepared statements.

question: why did creating a knowledge article return deduplicated instead of a new id
source: hand-authored from the knowledge wiki domain skill

corpus.title: The novelty gate returns a duplicate verdict
corpus.body: When a near identical article already exists the novelty gate returns a duplicate verdict, creates nothing, and points at the existing article id to update instead.

corpus.title: High overlap is gated to a draft
corpus.body: A proposal with high but not identical overlap is created as a draft carrying its near neighbours in metadata so an agent can merge or publish it.

corpus.title: Idempotency key on article create
corpus.body: A stable high entropy idempotency key makes a retried create a no op that returns the existing article reference.

corpus.title: Same title with a different body conflicts
corpus.body: Creating an article with an existing title but a different body returns a title conflict that must not be retried.

question: should I store this as agent memory or a knowledge article
source: hand-authored from the agent memory docs

corpus.title: Choosing between agent memory and the knowledge wiki
corpus.body: Store a fact only you need to recall about your own task as agent memory; store an insight worth another agent reading as a knowledge article.

corpus.title: Agent memory scope is derived from the key
corpus.body: Agent memory is private to the tenant and subject pair derived from the calling key, so the caller never passes a tenant id.

corpus.title: Session turns are pruned by time to live
corpus.body: Short term session turns are chronological and pruned by a time to live sweep rather than embedded and recalled semantically.

corpus.title: Structured access to live rows
corpus.body: The context retriever gives governed structured access to live project and story rows through declared entities.

question: how do I expose a live table to agents as a filterable tool
source: hand-authored from the context retriever docs

corpus.title: Declare an entity to generate retriever tools
corpus.body: A tenant admin declares an entity over the allowlisted fields, and the generator emits per entity filter and search tools appended to the tool list.

corpus.title: Every retriever query is parameterized and audited
corpus.body: A retriever query is parameterized, dual tenant scoped, allowlist rechecked at execute time, shaped to declared columns, and audited fail closed.

corpus.title: Defining an entity is a security root
corpus.body: Declaring an entity requires a user role key with a human anchor, while querying one only requires authentication.

corpus.title: Browsing the knowledge catalog
corpus.body: The knowledge index browses lightweight article metadata grouped by category with deterministic pagination.

question: how do I paginate a large article list without offset
source: hand-authored from the pagination patterns

corpus.title: Keyset pagination with an opaque cursor
corpus.body: Keyset pagination encodes the last row sort key into an opaque cursor so a deep page does not degrade the way an offset scan does.

corpus.title: The composite index a keyset page needs
corpus.body: A deep keyset page needs a composite index whose leading columns match the sort key exactly or the planner falls back to a sort over the corpus.

corpus.title: Relevance pagination is capped by the pool
corpus.body: Relevance search results come from a capped candidate pool, so a page deeper than the pool returns nothing.

corpus.title: Total count scope depends on the search mode
corpus.body: The reported total count means different things per mode, so read the total count scope before sizing a corpus from it.

question: how are token usage budgets and cost anomalies handled
source: hand-authored from the token usage context

corpus.title: Token usage rolls up into per model cost
corpus.body: Reported input and output token counts roll up into a per model cost so agent and model strategy can be compared over time.

corpus.title: Resolving a cost anomaly requires a human
corpus.body: Budget corrections and cost anomaly resolution stay at the user role because they are custody critical and not reversible by an agent.

corpus.title: Reporting token usage with a story report
corpus.body: The reviewer passes the token usage measurements when reporting a story so the cost rollup attributes them to the implementing agent.

corpus.title: Local rate limiting of embedding calls
corpus.body: An admission gate rate limits embedding calls locally and surfaces a rate limited reason instead of calling the provider.

question: what is the human anchor at tenant signup
source: hand-authored from chain of custody v2 section 2.1

corpus.title: WebAuthn roots a tenant in a human and a hardware key
corpus.body: Tenant signup enrolls a WebAuthn authenticator so the tenant is anchored to a human holding hardware, which every later custody claim inherits.

corpus.title: The signup ceremony is atomic
corpus.body: The signup ceremony wraps tenant creation, authenticator enrollment, and audit entries in one transaction so a failed attestation rolls everything back.

corpus.title: Agent rooted tenants have a lower trust tier
corpus.body: A tenant without a human anchor carries the agent rooted trust tier and cannot attach work projects.

corpus.title: Session cookie flags
corpus.body: Session cookies are set with the secure and http only flags in every environment that terminates TLS.

question: how do I make several inserts atomic and get a useful failure reason
source: hand-authored from the ecto patterns skill

corpus.title: Ecto.Multi names each step so failures are precise
corpus.body: Ecto.Multi runs named steps in one transaction and returns the failing step name with its changeset, so a caller can report exactly which insert failed.

corpus.title: Per index step names for a batch insert
corpus.body: Naming each batch step with its index lets a bulk operation report which item failed while still rolling back the whole transaction.

corpus.title: insert_all bypasses changesets
corpus.body: insert_all skips changesets and autogenerated timestamps, so validate first and set the timestamps explicitly.

corpus.title: Preload versus join preload
corpus.body: A separate preload uses less memory for a has many association than a join preload, which can multiply rows.

question: where should a liveview load its data
source: hand-authored from the phoenix thinking skill

corpus.title: Load data in handle_params not mount
corpus.body: mount runs twice, once for the http request and once for the websocket connect, so every database query belongs in handle_params instead.

corpus.title: What mount is for
corpus.body: mount sets empty assigns, subscribes to topics, and establishes defaults; it never queries the database.

corpus.title: Streams avoid memory ballooning
corpus.body: Use a stream for a collection so the socket does not hold every row, and give the container a dom id with a stream update.

corpus.title: terminate does not fire without trap exit
corpus.body: A liveview terminate callback only runs when the process traps exits, so cleanup belongs in a monitoring process.

question: when should I supersede versus merge two conflicting articles
source: hand-authored from the conflict resolution playbook

corpus.title: Supersede when one article clearly wins
corpus.body: Supersede retires the losing article behind a reversible link when one of the two is clearly correct against the live system.

corpus.title: Merge produces a draft, never a publish
corpus.body: Merging two complementary articles produces a new draft that a human or agent reviews before publishing, so nothing is auto published.

corpus.title: Dismiss a false positive conflict
corpus.body: Dismiss the conflict when the two articles only look similar and neither contradicts the other.

corpus.title: Archiving an article is a soft delete
corpus.body: Archiving sets the status to archived and retains the row, which is why it is reversible and available at agent role.

question: why does bulk delete of knowledge articles require a user role key
source: hand-authored from the KB content carve out

corpus.title: Set based bulk operations keep the human gate
corpus.body: A bulk delete mutates an unbounded set in one call and carries a hard delete path that destroys rows, so it stays at the user role.

corpus.title: Single article curation is agent role
corpus.body: Single article create, update, and archive are reversible and audited, so they are agent role curation rather than human gated.

corpus.title: Unpublishing a single article
corpus.body: Single article unpublish stays at the user role while publish sits at the orchestrator role.

corpus.title: Every curation mutation is audited
corpus.body: Curation mutations are recorded in the append only hash chained audit log and the per tenant curation log when enabled.

question: how does the audit log prove it was not rewritten
source: hand-authored from the audit chain context

corpus.title: The audit log is hash chained
corpus.body: Each audit entry carries the hash of its predecessor, so rewriting any earlier entry breaks every hash after it.

corpus.title: Signed tree heads witness the chain
corpus.body: A signed tree head periodically commits to the whole chain and is witnessed externally, so a divergent head halts the system.

corpus.title: Story history is an immutable event log
corpus.body: The story history endpoint returns the immutable event log so an observer can replay the decision chain.

corpus.title: Polling the change feed
corpus.body: An external observer polls the change feed since a cursor to see every state transition across a project.

question: which http client should a new integration use
source: hand-authored from the integration patterns skill

corpus.title: Use Req for every http client
corpus.body: Every outbound http integration uses Req rather than Tesla or HTTPoison, with one client builder function and transient retry.

corpus.title: Only retry server errors and network faults
corpus.body: Retry transient failures such as five hundreds and network faults; retrying a four hundred hides a real client error.

corpus.title: Caching an oauth token
corpus.body: Cache the oauth token with a short expiry buffer and take a lock before refreshing so nodes do not stampede the token endpoint.

corpus.title: Circuit breaker states
corpus.body: A circuit breaker moves from closed to open after a failure threshold and to half open after a reset timeout.

question: what are the story statuses from pending to verified
source: hand-authored from the story lifecycle docs

corpus.title: The story status progression
corpus.body: A story moves from pending to contracted to assigned to implementing to reported done to verified, and each transition has its own endpoint.

corpus.title: Claiming uses pessimistic locking
corpus.body: Claiming a contracted story takes a row lock so two agents cannot claim the same story concurrently.

corpus.title: Verification is exact role gated
corpus.body: Verify and reject are gated to the exact orchestrator role, so a user or superadmin key cannot verify.

corpus.title: Contracting checks the title and criteria count
corpus.body: Contracting a story requires the exact title and acceptance criteria count so a silent misclaim is impossible.

question: what vector dimension do article embeddings use
source: hand-authored from the embedding config

corpus.title: Article embeddings are configured to a fixed dimension
corpus.body: The embedding dimension is a single configuration value and the article changeset validates that any stored vector matches it exactly.

corpus.title: Only one changeset may write the embedding
corpus.body: The embedding field is excluded from the normal cast fields so only the dedicated embedding changeset can set or clear it.

corpus.title: The embedding content hash skips paid recomputation
corpus.body: A hash of the embedded text lets the worker skip calling the paid provider again when a job retries.

corpus.title: The HNSW index name drifts between environments
corpus.body: The vector index name differs between test and production, so detection probes the index access method instead of the name.

question: what happens to an outbound call when egress is blocked
source: hand-authored from the egress policy epic

corpus.title: A blocked egress degrades the response explicitly
corpus.body: When egress policy blocks the provider call the response is explicitly labelled with an egress blocked reason and the offending endpoint rather than an empty result.

corpus.title: Webhook delivery obeys the same egress policy
corpus.body: Webhook delivery runs under the single egress policy so no outbound path can bypass the allowlist.

corpus.title: Excluded tiers is reserved in the degraded meta
corpus.body: The degraded response carries a reserved excluded tiers field so the contract stays stable when encrypted bodies leave the index.

corpus.title: Trusting a custom certificate authority
corpus.body: Point the node extra ca certs variable at the bundle instead of disabling certificate verification.

question: what does the full quality gate run before a commit
source: hand-authored from mix.exs precommit

corpus.title: The precommit alias is the full quality gate
corpus.body: The precommit alias compiles with warnings as errors, checks unused dependencies, checks formatting, runs credo strict, audits dependencies, runs dialyzer, and runs the tests.

corpus.title: Never bypass the commit hooks
corpus.body: The no verify flag is forbidden, so a failing hook is fixed rather than skipped.

corpus.title: Do not suppress dialyzer with module attributes
corpus.body: Dialyzer warnings are fixed at the root cause; the ignore file carries only known upstream issues.

corpus.title: The dependency cache key includes config
corpus.body: The continuous integration cache key includes the config files so a config change forces a clean recompile of config sensitive dependencies.

question: how is tenant id set on a new record
source: hand-authored from the multi tenancy rules

corpus.title: tenant id is never cast from parameters
corpus.body: The tenant id is set programmatically on the struct and never appears in a changeset cast, so a client cannot choose another tenant.

corpus.title: Every context function takes the tenant first
corpus.body: Context functions take the tenant id as their first argument so scoping is impossible to forget at a call site.

corpus.title: Every context test asserts tenant isolation
corpus.body: Each context test includes a case proving one tenant cannot read another tenant rows.

corpus.title: Global tables have no tenant column
corpus.body: Only the tenants table and a small set of global tables omit the tenant column.

question: how does hybrid search decide between a curated and a retrieved answer
source: hand-authored from the hybrid retrieval docs

corpus.title: Curated wins only on absolute confidence and margin
corpus.body: A curated source wins only when its absolute confidence clears a scale matched threshold, beats the best retrieved candidate by a margin, and is still authoritative.

corpus.title: Both provenance branches share one response shape
corpus.body: The curated and retrieved branches return identical result and meta key sets, so a caller branches on the provenance field alone.

corpus.title: Progressive disclosure browses cheap stubs
corpus.body: Progressive disclosure returns compact stubs with one hop of hub enrichment before a full body drill into a chosen stub.

corpus.title: A sparse pool must not promote a wrong curated doc
corpus.body: A near but wrong curated document never wins by default merely because the retrieved pool is sparse.
